topPRs.title: ci: speed up kona-host-client-offline-cannon by about 5 min
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
**Metrics** (CircleCI, xlarge.gen2 machine)

| | develop's job | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `kona-host-client-offline-cannon` | 785, 807 s (25 recent PR runs: median 788 s) | 458, 467 s with a warm cache. 683 s before develop has written one |
| docker env image build in that job | 175-177 s | 3-56 s |
| native kona-host build | 292-300 s | 74-75 s warm (310 s cold) |
| client ELF build, cannon run | 158-164 s, 79-80 s | same |
| `kona-build-fpvm-cannon-client` | 348 s | 187 s |

- Modeled on 25 recent runs each, rust-ci finishes at 13.4 min instead of 14.9 for PRs and 13.1 instead of 14.8 for the queue. After that, cargo-hack, rust-tests and udeps set its end.
- About 40 vCPU-min less per rust-ci pipeline from this job, about 20 more from `kona-build-fpvm-cannon-client` when its env image misses.
- Bench pipeline 139470: develop's job and this PR's side by side, same commit, a `rust/kona` change so the env image misses as it does on real PRs. The warm copies primed a local-disk sccache with a different kona-host source, wiped `rust/target`, then ran the real steps (2700 hits, 1 miss), because a branch can't write the shared cache.

**What changes**
- `build-kona-env` builds `cannon-repro.dockerfile` to `--target kona-build-env`, and that stage ended with the full kona-client ELF build. `lint-cannon` and `build-cannon-client` then build again in `docker run`, so every env image miss built the ELFs twice. The ELF build moves to its own stage that only the prestate build uses.
- This job runs on a machine executor, which has no sccache, so `rust-sccache-setup` skipped it and kona-host built cold every run. It now installs the release the Rust base image ships (0.18.0), checked against upstream's sha256.

**Why it's safe**
- Same client: `kona-client` and `kona-client-int` ELFs and the Cannon `state.bin.gz` are byte-identical in all five bench copies, old and new. The Cannon run validates block 47600000 and exits 0 in every copy.
- Same prestates: `kona-client` 0x034e09d1...f07f4d and `kona-client-int` 0x030e7d01...714b71, from develop 8b081c14f7, the old Dockerfile and the new one. The prestate build runs the same RUN on the same layers.
- Same host: still the dev profile, built by the same recipe. sccache only caches it.
- Cache writes stay develop-only (#21227). `RUSTC_WRAPPER` doesn't reach the Docker client build or the Go cannon build.
- Until the first develop run after merge writes this job's entries, kona-host builds cold (about 15 s slower). The job is still faster then, because of the Dockerfile fix.
- Like every other Rust job, this one now fails if sccache can't start, rather than building without it.
